newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Smith says spending control best for high NZD.
newsitem.headline: Smith says spending control best for high NZD.

text.p: New Zealand's International Trade Minister Lockwood Smith on Thursday acknowledged the pain caused by the high New Zealand dollar, but said restraining government spending was the only sure way to curb it.

"While I acknowledge the pain caused by our dollar's strength, I have seen no evidence that any measures to curb that strength would be guaranteed of success, apart from ensuring that excessive government spending doesn't put too much pressure on monetary policy," Smith said in a prepared speech.

"I believe the government's firm, anti-inflationary stance provides the best platform for long term economic stability and growth," he said at the opening of new plant at glass manufacturer and exporter Pilkington New Zealand.

The government has been under pressure from farming and exporting lobby groups to reduce the extra spending it has planned for the next three years, including NZ$100 million set aside to promote business and exports, in order to take the pressure off the dollar.

The centre-right National-New Zealand First coalition has said it will increase spending by $1.2 billion in the 1997/98 year, by $1.7 billion in 1998/99 and $2.1 billion in 1999/2000 while maintaining surpluses of between two percent and three percent of GDP.
Smith said New Zealand would continue to push for trade liberalisation through the World Trade Organisation.
